audit.why: 53.64% over 220 games. The chart gives Ziggs levels 1-3 and level 6 with Camille only on the Skill stages, which reads harsh for a 53% lane — but the prose is explicit that the lane flips hard from level 2 onward and that Camille's problem is a stalled game rather than the lane itself. The shape holds together.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is written as 'the lane-ender' with the only counterplay named being Satchel Charge. Mega Inferno Bomb is never mentioned in the matchup — the late section refers to 'his global R' without naming it.
audit.why: Mega Inferno Bomb is 120s at rank 1 down to 70s, and it is the reason a Ziggs who survives the level-6 all-in still threatens the wave, the plates and a low-health Camille from off-screen. Naming Camille's arena as a lane-ender while leaving his own ultimate unnamed at the same stage tells the reader only one side of level 6.
audit.corrected: Mega Inferno Bomb named with its 120s cooldown at level 6 and in late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's defect stands: no Ziggs ability is named. The matchup runs on 'his Q bomb', 'the E minefield', 'his Satchel' and 'his global R'. Short Fuse is absent entirely. Camille's passive is written as 'Adaptive Defense' and her R without its article.
audit.why: Riot's kit is Short Fuse (P), Bouncing Bomb (Q), Satchel Charge (W), Hexplosive Minefield (E), Mega Inferno Bomb (R). Short Fuse is the one that matters most and is missing: it periodically empowers his next basic attack, so in the melee-range moments this matchup keeps engineering, his biggest single hit comes off an auto rather than a spell — and the charge is the tell. _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this as an auto-reset burst tell for this pairing. The cooldown behind the central instruction is also unstated: Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 down to 12s, which is what makes 'bait the Satchel, then commit' a real plan rather than a hope, and Bouncing Bomb at 6s is what makes the poke phase unwinnable before level 2.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named; Short Fuse added as the empowered-auto tell; Satchel Charge's 20s and Bouncing Bomb's 6s written in; Adaptive Defenses and The Hextech Ultimatum given their real names.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait his Satchel knockback with a feinted E, then commit while it's on cooldown' and 'force the all-in every time E and R are up' name three cooldowns and give none.
audit.why: Satchel Charge at 20s against Hookshot's 16s is the single favourable number in the early game — her engage returns before his displacement does. That is the mechanical justification for the entire feint-then-commit plan the matchup is built around, and it is currently asserted without support.
audit.corrected: 20s vs 16s written into wants.you[2] and mid.

audit.why: wants.foe[1] contains the best line in the matchup and it is correct: Ziggs can lay Hexplosive Minefield on the wall Camille wants to grapple from. Against a champion whose engage requires terrain, denying the approach to the terrain is better counterplay than trying to answer the dash itself, and very little of this champion's data reaches that level of specificity.

edits.before: Level 1 is his — a single Q bomb out-ranges everything you have and your one ability does nothing back, so soak last-hits and don't walk into the minefield to contest. At 2 you get your E grapple and a Q point; now you can threaten a wall-dash and step up. Eat one bomb on your Adaptive Defense shield rather than your health bar, and respect that his Satchel can both knock you out of a dash and reposition him short distances — but it won't save him once you're locked on.
edits.after: Level 1 is his — Bouncing Bomb out-ranges everything you have on a 6s cooldown and your one ability answers nothing, so soak last-hits and stay out of Hexplosive Minefield. At 2 you get Hookshot and a Q point and can threaten a wall-dash. Adaptive Defenses only shields you once your own attack lands, so it is not cover for the poke phase — and watch Short Fuse, which empowers his next auto for his biggest single hit up close.

edits.before: This is where it flips hard. With Q's true-damage second hit and your E gap-close you punish him the instant he steps up to poke — grapple in (off a wall when you can for the longer dash and stun), W-slash the outer edge for the slow and heal, then the Q recast for the burst. Bait his Satchel knockback by feinting the dash, then commit when it's down — without it he has only flash and his short Satchel hop to peel you off. At 6 your R seals it: arena him and his range, minefield, and reposition all go dead.
edits.after: This is where it flips hard. With Q's true-damage second hit and your Hookshot gap-close you punish him the instant he steps up to poke — grapple in off a wall for the longer dash and knockup, W-slash the outer edge for the slow and heal, then the Q recast for the burst. Feint the dash to bait Satchel Charge: it is 20s to your 16s, so your engage comes back first, and without it he has only Flash. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum seals the lane, but he still holds a 120s Mega Inferno Bomb for the wave.

edits.before: You owned the lane, but full-build Ziggs is a problem if you let the game stall — at siege range his Q poke and E zone control mean he never has to face you 1v1, and his global R picks off your low team. Your job is to have already snowballed off your Level 6 R kills: take his tower, roam, and force fights where your E-into-R isolates him from his peel before he pokes your team apart. If it goes 40 minutes even, he out-ranges you — close it on your spike.
